settlement.explanation: External production limits reduce the damage ceiling first. Only production below that ceiling is charged.

capacity.penaltyWarning: This is a per-turn commitment. Production below the damage ceiling incurs shortfall damages equal to {penaltyPercent}% of the market value of each missing unit.

negotiation.intro: Private off-market commodity negotiations. Either CEO can make the opening offer, send a counter-offer, or accept the current terms. Either party can cancel.
negotiation.openingHelp: The other corporation must accept or counter before the contract starts.
negotiation.counterpartyHelp: Any player-run corporation, including foreign ones, can be a counterparty.
negotiation.freightHelp: Freight is haulage capacity based in one state. The contract reserves the supplier's plants there for the buyer's plants in the same state.
negotiation.buyerFreightHelp: The supplier's capacity is checked when they review the offer.
negotiation.volumeHelp: Units/turn reserved for the buyer. Anything your sectors make above this still sells on the open market as normal.
negotiation.priceHelp: At most ±{band}% of market price. Positive favours the supplier; negative favours the buyer.
negotiation.termHelp: Leave blank for an open-ended agreement. Fixed terms run for {min} to {max} turns after acceptance.
negotiation.acceptOrCounter: Accept this offer or send a counter-offer.
negotiation.waiting: Waiting for the counterparty to respond.

validation.positiveVolume: Volume cap must be a positive number
validation.priceBand: Price must be within ±{band}% of market
validation.freightState: Select the state this freight contract is fulfilled from

sectorInvestment.recoveryExplanation: Park surplus capacity while keeping a smaller operation running. Parked plants pay reduced upkeep. You keep the plants and can reopen them for free. Production, staffing and upkeep adjust next turn; supply commitments still apply.
sectorInvestment.mothballHelp: Mothball all capacity or park just a share below. Cold capacity pays {percent}% of its anchored maintenance basis and produces nothing. Normal depreciation continues.
sectorInvestment.cancelHelp: Cancellation returns 75% of the cost of the capacity still under construction. Delivered capacity is kept.
sectorInvestment.strandedOptions: Options: park surplus capacity in the Plant panel, change to a strategy with stronger demand, stockpile storable goods during a temporary glut, or sell the sector. Growing capacity will help only where buyers can absorb it.
sectorInvestment.expansionDiscountHelp: New ordinary expansion receives this build-cost reduction. Founder pricing is separate.
sectorInvestment.rampHelp: Capacity arrives gradually from next turn until the build completes. Existing paid orders keep their original schedule.
sectorInvestment.noForecast: A cash-return scenario needs current operating figures after temporary market support has ended. It is unavailable during market support, retooling, or while those figures are missing or stale.
sectorInvestment.cashReturn: of the build cost returned as cash
sectorInvestment.assumptions: Holds last turn's prices, production pace, sales share and costs constant. Assumes existing cash funds the build; borrowing costs and returns forgone elsewhere are excluded. Capacity and strategy changes made since that turn are not included. Additional sales are capped by measured unmet demand; unwanted output still incurs production costs. Includes the construction ramp, physical depreciation, idle upkeep and freight. Excludes receipts from selling previously stored inventory. Allocates today's corporation overhead, including R&D, proportionally; taxes positive income at {tax}%. Reserves cash for replacement. Prices, demand, policies, staffing and competitors can change. Remaining value is depreciated construction spend, excludes transfer fees and is not a cash sale quote. Returns are cumulative, not annualized.
sectorInvestment.deductions96: Over 96 turns: overhead {overhead}, tax {tax}, replacement reserve {replacement}.
sectorInvestment.noDemand: There is no measured unmet demand for this output mix. This scenario gives new capacity no additional sales. A new strategy, better delivery or winning customers could change that.
